$comment: WHAT LEVEL AM I. Rebuilt 2026-08-22, the same day the first version shipped, because he read it
and said: "I do think that maybe we're being too strict."
He was right, and the arithmetic says how wrong it was. The first version derived its lower
tiers as multiples of the US Masters national qualifying time. USMS builds that qualifying time
as roughly the tenth-fastest time in the country plus 10 to 15%. Multiplying an elite standard
by a small factor keeps you in elite territory: "Club" came out meaning within 1.40x of the
tenth fastest man in the United States, and the entire recreational range, which is where he
and nearly every adult swimmer lives, collapsed into two bands.
SEVEN TIERS NOW, and the top three are still the sourced ones. The bottom four are ours, spaced
to give the recreational range the room it actually occupies. Tier NAMES follow the set he had
already been using in a separate conversation, because he has a feel for them and inventing a
seventh vocabulary would only make the app harder to read.
ONE THING HE HAD WRONG, AND IT IS SMALL. The table he was reading was LONG course, 50 m pool.
His pool is 25 m and freestyle is about 3% faster short course, so reading his own times
straight off a long-course table flattered him by roughly half a tier. Corrected, he is Fitness
at 100 and 1500 and Club at 200 and 400, which is what he said he was.
COURSE DISCIPLINE. Everything sourced here is short course 25 m, his own pool, EXCEPT the
qualifying row, which is long course because USMS publishes no short-course-metres standard.
That row is flagged in its own provenance value so it can never be read as like for like.
3 km AND 5 km ARE NOT POOL EVENTS. No tier table exists for them at any level, so they are
extrapolated from the 1500 and marked as such at every tier. The 5 km factor is anchored to the
only real relationship available: an open-water world championship 5 km of about 51:29 against
a 1500 m short-course world record of 14:06.88.
WHY THERE IS STILL NO 25 m OR 50 m PERSONAL BEST. The tier table now covers 50 m, but he has no
time for it. Samsung records no best under 100 m, and deriving one from single lengths does not
survive the data: the fastest length ever recorded is 9.03 s, faster than a world-record 25 m
split, and filtering the sensor miscounts moves the answer from 14.42 s to 18.55 s depending on
where the threshold goes.

meta.courseNote: Short course, 25 m pool. The same pool he swims in.

distanceNotes.3000: Not a pool event. Extrapolated from the 1500 at 2.10x.
distanceNotes.5000: Not a pool event. Extrapolated from the 1500 at 3.65x, the ratio between an open-water world championship 5 km (about 51:29) and the 1500 m short-course world record (14:06.88). Open water has no walls and a mass start, so treat it as a scale marker.

sources.label: Masters world records, SCM, as of 2025-09-02
sources.note: World Aquatics. Age group 35-39 read out of the PDF directly.

sources.label: US Masters Swimming Top 10, 2025, SCM, men 35-39
sources.note: The tenth-place time is a real swimmer in his age group this year, which is a better anchor than a record nobody approaches.

sources.label: US Masters national qualifying times, men 35-39
sources.note: LONG course, 50 m. USMS publishes no short-course-metres qualifying standard. Roughly the tenth-fastest time in the country plus 10 to 15%.

sources.label: Open water 5 km world championship result
sources.note: Used only to anchor how much a 5 km slows against a 1500.

sources.label: Short course to long course conversion, freestyle
sources.note: Freestyle short course metres is about 3% faster than long course. This is why reading his times off a long-course table flattered him.

tiers.name: World class
tiers.what: The fastest man aged 35 to 39 on record, anywhere in the world.

tiers.name: High performance
tiers.what: Tenth fastest in the United States in 2025 in this age group. A real swimmer, this year, not a record.

tiers.name: Competitive
tiers.what: Fast enough to enter the US Masters national championships. Long course, so read it as a scale marker rather than a target in your pool.

tiers.name: Club
tiers.what: Trains with a squad and races. Set at 1.25x the qualifying time. That multiplier is a choice, not a finding.

tiers.name: Fitness
tiers.what: Swims two or three times a week on purpose, works on technique, is not racing. This is where you are.

tiers.name: Recreational
tiers.what: Swims laps regularly with no plan behind it.

tiers.name: First timer
tiers.what: Can get to the other end, at whatever pace. Deliberately not a time: at this stage the only question is whether you finish the length.

profileNote: His four bests score 113, 137, 154 and 130 against the age-matched world record at 100, 200,
400 and 1500. That is an unusually EVEN profile, and it tilts towards distance: he is
relatively strongest at 400 m and relatively weakest at 100 m.
The stroke data says the same thing from the other side. He takes about 9 stroke cycles per
25 m at roughly 18 cycles a minute, which is a long, slow, glide-heavy stroke. That is an engine
